summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with advanced HIV (CD4 count 6) and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for worsening right-sided headache, dizziness, and hypotension following self-discontinuation of increased-dose gabapentin. She had a history of herpes zoster ophthalmicus with postherpetic neuralgia and presented with facial lesions and severe pruritus. Initial evaluation revealed leukopenia, hypotension responsive to fluids, and transient atrial fibrillation. Imaging showed no acute intracranial abnormality but confirmed chronic calcifications related to renal disease. She was managed in the ICU initially with broad-spectrum antibiotics and acyclovir, later discontinued due to lack of infection evidence. Her pain was transitioned from gabapentin to amitriptyline, and pruritus was treated with fexofenadine. Preventive antibiotics (Bactrim and azithromycin) were restarted due to profound immunosuppression. She tolerated hemodialysis without complications, remained stable, and was discharged home with improved symptoms and a plan for ongoing outpatient care.
